newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard claimed yesterday that to leave Australia's media ownership rules as they are would leave the John Fairfax publishing group "inherently unstable", with no one really running the company. Howard's comments open the door for Kerr Packer's bid to take control of Fairfax. Page 1.

AMP Society managing director and chief executive officer George Trumbull said yesterday the group is considering a generous offer of making share handouts to management and staff, a move that may add a further A$1 billion to the value of its A$9 billion loat. Trumbull added that more capital could be raised through the issue of shares to the public and institutional investors. Page 1.

Australia's most successful gold explorer, Joe Gutnick, yesterday announced another gold discovery. The find resulted from drilling in an area 40 kilometres north of Kalgoorlie in Western Australia which had been investigated by prospectors for the past 10 years, and find could yield a further five million ounces. Page 19.

BHP directors said yesterday they believe the company should have closed the Newcastle steelworks two years ago, and also revealed they had recently considered selling the entire steel division. As BHP spent the day defending their decision to close the Newcastle plant in 1999, investors supported the decision, with shares rising a further 21.5 cents to A$18.08. Page 20.

Brierley Investments chairman Bob Matthew said yesterday there was no rift between BIL and its major shareholder, the Singapore-based Delham syndicate, with whom it is working on several deals. Matthew said BIL is not looking at selling any major Australan investments, but is hoping for greater value from its entire portfolio. Page 20.

Mining and consumer products assisted ICI Australia Ltd yesterday in its 19.5 per cent rise in first-half earnings, offsetting a drop in chemicals and plastics prices. The group enjoyed a profit of A$110.7 million in the half-year to March, the result of significant productivity gains in an overall weak Australian market. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Ansett Australia's new executive chairman Rod Eddington said yesterday the airline must amend its poor business to ensure its medium to long term survival. While Eddington acknowledged the airline was "excellent", with committed staff dedicated to customer service, he said this was not enough to generate profits. Page 21.

A new study, called ClipCare and launched in 1995 by Australia's leading wool broker Elders Ltd, will show wool growers that attention to quality can mean extra dollars. The study, coming as wool prices continue to surge, showed that those in the industry who took part in a quality-assurance program have received up to 16 cents a kilogram more for their wool. Page 21.

In its move to become an aggressive international finance house, AMP Society announced yesterday it will move into banking and has committed itself to demutualisation. Managing director George Trumbull will meet next week with the Reserve Bank as part ofthe plan to form an AMP Bank and move its focus into fund management, personal financial services and risk management. Page 21.

The Australian Stock Exchange yesterday refused Star Mining Corp NL's bid to have its shares relisted, despite further backing for Star from South African mining giant JCI Ltd. Star's shares were suspended in early April after a Russian court cast doubt ver the legal title to the Sukhoi Log gold project in Siberia, in which Star holds a 49 per cent interest. Page 23.

BHP Steel chief executive Ron McNeilly said yesterday the steel division would have been in danger of collapsing had the decision to close the Newcastle plant not been made. McNeilly said maintaining steel making in Newcastle would have spelt the demise of the Whyalla operations and threatened the future of the Port Kembla plant. Page 23.

Petroz NL managing director Rod Brown said yesterday the company - along with six partners, including BHP, Santos and Phillips Petroleum - is looking at investing A$300 million in the Undan-Bayu gas field in the Timor Sea, using bank debt and possible euity raising. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking after AMP Society's annual general meeting yesterday, managing director George Trumbull said he will meet with Reserve Bank officials next week to discuss the process of applying for a banking licence. The AMP board will then consider whether tofile a formal application. Page 33.

Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd made no official comment last night concerning rumours the Kerry Packer-owned company was set to call off its A$342 million offer the buy management control and a 10 per cent share of the Sydney Harbour Casino from the Unitd States-based Showboat Inc. Page 33.

Under a deal worth more than A$1.3 billion, AMP Society has combined with United Kingdom airport company BAA plc, and is set to win the bid to buy the Melbourne Airport. The group appears to have just topped the bidding for Australia's second busiest airort, which was being competed by a Macquarie Bank-led consortium. Page 33.

Visa International looks set to beat its main rival MasterCard in the race to introduce the first multi-application smart card to Australia. Following an agreement yesterday with Card Technologies Australia, Visa International expects its Visa Cash-CiT card here before the end of the year, and in common use by 2000. Page 35.

The Federal Government is not expected to react favourably to moves by New Zealand company Brierley Investments to create a special "Australian" company in order to maintain its 19.9 per cent stake in John Fairfax Holdings. The move would allow Brierley to meet foreign ownership rules, which restrict foreign owners to a 25 per cent stake in a major newspaper. Page 35.

Under a move that would require approval from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Ansett and its 50 per cent shareholder Air New Zealand are looking at merging a wide range of their key day-to-day operations, such as information technology Page 35.
THE AGE

AMP Society managing director George Trumbull, speaking after the company's annual meeting yesterday, revealed he would meet Reserve Bank officials next week to apply for a banking licence for AMP in the lead up to the company's demutualisation in November. Page B1.

Richard Pratt's Visy Industries has used A$500 million in long-term funds raised from a United States corporate bond issue, believed to be the biggest financing completed by a privately owned Australian company, to replace loans to the company from Austraian banks. Page B1.

Speaking publicly for the first time yesterday, Ansett executive chairman Rod Eddington said he hopes to revive the loss making airline by gaining clearance from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission for closer ties between Ansett and Air NewZealand and selling off non-core businesses, including Hayman Island, for which the airline would be prepared to take a big loss. Page B1.

Following Wall Street's second highest point gain in history, the Australian All Ordinaries index hit the 2500 mark for the first time in two months yesterday, but closed at 2488. While local bond prices rose, dealers were disappointed the surge on Wall treet had not inspired greater gains. Page B1.

Following a poor production performance in the March quarter, Newcrest Mining has reported promising exploration results from its Backdoor and Ridgeway prospects. Newcrest's production was down from 137,912 ounces to 102,140, mainly due to heavy rains inWestern Australia, which resulted in the six week closure of the Telfer project. Page B2.

Alan Birchmore, a major shareholder in West Australian gold miner St Barbara Mines, will push for a voluntary liquidation of the company in a desperate attempt to end internal problems. Birchmore says the move will give shareholders the chance to get at east A$1.00 or more for each of their shares, compared to yesterday's rate of 63 cents. Page B2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
